choices.text: A magnet pulls it, because it is a metal
A magnet does not pull it in the way iron is pulled, because a magnet only pulls iron and a few metals
A magnet pushes it away, because like poles repel

questions.feedback: That trap answer is the one to unlearn: A magnet attracts every kind of metal. Reteach point: Magnets ignore most things: they only pull iron and a few metals. Check scene s4: the warning is that a magnet does not attract every metal - test metals one by one instead of assuming.
questions.misconception: A magnet attracts every kind of metal.
questions.prompt: A pupil holds a magnet near an aluminium can and expects it to stick. What should they expect instead?

questions.answer: It is a push: the foot pushes the ball away.
questions.feedback: Scene s1 fixes the sorting: a push moves something away from you and a pull brings it closer - the kicked ball moves away, so it is a push.
questions.prompt: Kicking a football: is this a push or a pull? Give the reason.

choices.text: Gravity switches off on a smooth surface
There is less friction on the smooth surface, so less rubbing force slows the block
A smooth surface pushes the block forwards

questions.feedback: Scene s2 fixes the idea: friction is the rubbing force that fights sliding - a rough surface rubs more, a smooth surface rubs less, so the block keeps sliding for longer.
questions.prompt: Why does a block slide further on a smooth floor than on a rough floor?

questions.answer: They repel: like poles push each other apart.
questions.feedback: Scene s4 fixes the rule: N facing N means like poles, and like poles repel - the magnets push apart instead of snapping together.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, say what two magnets do when the north pole of one faces the north pole of the other.
